title: Other uptown trumpeters and the legitimate bands of Kimball and Robichaud
summary: Brief answers on obscure trumpeters, then Andrew Kimball and John Robichaud's Guy Lombardo-style legitimate dance bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask about a couple other uptown trumpet players that nobody seems to know anything much about him, like Edward Clam. Edward Clam.
Well, he was from, I think, Cinderella, La Platt, somewhere out there. Came down the river. Yeah, well, he was sensational. He was a fair. He was a fair kind of player.

And another fellow, Ned. I never heard that's his last name or first name. Do you remember anything about him? Ned. Ned, you see. Came after Bolden and there was some who played maybe a little bit with Frankie Doosman for a while. I don't even hear all those stories. I don't know what's the name.
I don't remember Ned. You don't remember Ned. But I remember Joe Johnson and, oh, who was the other guy?
Was Andrew Kimball very early in the way?

Andrew Kimball, yes. Andrew Kimball was always on the legitimate side though. He was. He was John Robichaud. John Robichaud, yeah. John Robichaud had a band, I'll say, more under the style of Guy Lombardo. Most everything he played was legitimate. It was good dance music but it was on the legitimate side. There was nothing hot about it. And Imperial was pretty much on that order. He played good music, good dance music, but it was not.
